evals.prompt: Build a CWP user-panel module where customers can see their top disk-using folders. Computing it needs root.
evals.expected_output: A user module plus root job queue; module never runs root commands itself.
expectations: Creates the three files: user_files/modules/<name>.php, users/cwp_lang/en/<name>.ini and the Twig mod_<name>.html in the theme folder
Uses $_SESSION['username'] as the only identity and validates it; never takes the account from request parameters
Does not call shell_exec/exec/system or build shell strings in the module; privileged work goes through a job queue
Queue: module writes a strictly validated JSON job atomically into a root/panel-owned 0700 spool, not into the customer's home
A root cron/systemd processor re-validates file owner, size, JSON shape, user, action allowlist and args, and runs handlers with argument arrays
Module polls a result that is only returned to the job's own user
Uses the same-route AJAX convention (?module=<name>&acc=<action>), POST+CSRF for submit, JSON responses
Registers the module by adding a block to menuConf.php without replacing the whole file, and mentions enabling the feature for the package
Flags the undocumented parts (session keys, menuConf entry format, panel uid) as things to verify on the target CWP version

evals.prompt: My CWP user module reads a 'user' field from the POST body and then runs a root script for that user. Can you make it safe?
evals.expected_output: Rewrite that removes request-supplied identity and uses a queue.
expectations: Explains that identity must come from $_SESSION['username'], so any request-supplied user is a horizontal privilege escalation
Removes the direct root execution from the panel-facing code and introduces the spool-based job queue
Adds CSRF protection for the submit action and rate limiting / pending-job cap per user
Processor verifies the job's user against the file name and the real hosting account (uid, home directory) and rejects symlinks and oversized files
Never reads files from customer-writable locations as root without symlink checks
Adds a forged-job test plan (mismatched names, unknown actions, other users' ids, symlinks)

evals.prompt: Package my CWP user module so it survives CWP updates and can be installed and removed cleanly.
evals.expected_output: Installer/uninstaller/fix-module with menuConf patching and self-heal.
expectations: Installer and uninstaller are dry-run by default with --apply to execute
menuConf.php is patched by inserting a marked block (backup first, php -l on the result, rollback on failure), never by overwriting the file; uninstall deletes only the marked block
Handles chattr +i by unlocking only needed paths and restoring them via trap
Installs the Twig template into every listed theme and warns that the original theme is overwritten on CWP updates
Adds daily cron and /root/.cwp_autoupdate.sh self-heal calling the same fix routine
Sets up the spool directories with 0700 and the processor cron, and removes them on uninstall (keeping data unless --purge)
